title: Bury yourself
hook: bury your existence in the earth of obscurity, for what grows unburied doesn't flower (Hikam 11, paraphrased)
tomorrow: you asked and asked, and the answer is 'not yet.' now what?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ibn Ata'illah's first saying: if one slip wipes out your hope, you were leaning on your record. Rely on Him. Today, his advice about the dark.

Opening night of the school musical. Between scenes the lights drop to black, and a kid dressed all in black slips onstage, drags a staircase into place, and is gone before the lights come back up. Nobody claps for the staircase. At the bows, the leads get flowers. The crew is still in the wings, coiling cables. Ask the crew kid, and you might hear: one day I'll be out there. So here's the question the scene leaves hanging. Is staying unseen a loss, something to fix as fast as you can? Or is something happening back there that can't happen under the lights?
screen: `A KID IN BLACK MOVES THE STAIRS.` → `NOBODY CLAPS FOR THE STAIRCASE.` → `A LOSS, OR SOMETHING GROWING?`

segments.voice: Ibn Ata'illah, a Sufi teacher in Egypt, left a book of short sayings called al-Hikam, the wisdoms. Saying eleven, paraphrased: bury your existence in the earth of obscurity, because whatever sprouts without being buried doesn't come to full flower. It's a gardener's line. A seed left on top of the soil can sprout fast and then wilt, because nothing held it down long enough to grow roots. A buried seed looks like nothing is happening. That's exactly when the roots go down. His word for that earth is khumul: obscurity, being unknown, off the stage for a while. Readers of the Hikam hear it as a cure for the self's hunger to be seen. Show a good habit too early, and the applause can quietly become the reason for it. The same instinct lives in a hadith kept by al-Bukhari. Among the people God shades on a day when there is no other shade is someone who gives in charity so quietly that the left hand doesn't know what the right hand gave. Notice what Ibn Ata'illah isn't saying. He isn't saying never lead, never sing the solo, never be known. He's talking about order: roots first, in the dark; flowers later, if they come at all. So the crew kid isn't losing anything. The staircase still has to move, and something is growing back there that nobody is watching.
screen: `AL-HIKAM: SAYING ELEVEN.` · `A BURIED SEED GROWS ROOTS.` · `THE LEFT HAND DOESN'T KNOW.` · `ROOTS FIRST, FLOWERS LATER.` · then, large: `GROW IN THE DARK.`

segments.voice: Choose one good thing you could do this week that nobody will ever trace back to you: a dish washed before anyone wakes, a kind word passed along without your name on it. Decide exactly when you'll do it, and notice what part of you already wants to mention it later. Then let the plan sit, buried, while the breath comes and goes.
screen: `ONE GOOD THING, UNSIGNED.` · `WHEN, EXACTLY?` · `LET IT STAY BURIED.`

segments.voice: Bury yourself: Ibn Ata'illah's seed in the soil. Obscurity first, so the roots can go down before anything flowers.
Keep this one in your pocket: grow in the dark, where the roots don't need an audience. Three sayings of the Hikam so far.

screen: `DAY 1625 COUNTS.` → `IBN ATA'ILLAH · 3 OF 6.` → `TOMORROW: THE ANSWER IS 'NOT YET.' NOW WHAT?`

howItsDone: Following the hadith of the hand that gives so quietly the other hand doesn't know, Muslims try to keep some good deeds, such as charity or night prayer, private; Sufi teachers read Ibn Ata'illah's saying as training against the love of reputation.

fork.setup: your friends plan to hand out sandwiches at the shelter and film it for a 'giving day' post. the shelter didn't ask for a video. what fits Hikam 11?
options: film it; if it inspires one person, the post is the point.
hand out the sandwiches, skip the camera, and let it stay unseen.
don't go at all, since nobody's motives are completely pure.
fork.reveal: the saying doesn't cancel the deed; it cancels the stage. bury it, and let the roots grow where nobody is filming.

chat.meaning: Ibn Ata'illah's point is order: roots first, out of sight. Answering honestly where asked is fine; performing the deed for applause is the danger.
